thread:
Kira: Heads-up from pairing today: the python sample-app surfaced a blob of JSON when a user sent a malformed prompt. API returned 400 with {"code":"input.invalid", "message":"invalid characters in prompt"} but the UI showed 'Server error' and dumped the body. New devs are confused.
Ben: Oof. We need a clearer mapping for client-side input errors. 400 != generic server.
Sofia: Agreed. Proposal: unify exception taxonomy across SDKs and include a flat metadata map on each exception. Minimal classes: AuthError, RateLimitError, ClientInputError, ClientError, ServerError, StreamError, NetworkError.
Alex: +1 for ClientInputError for 4xx that are clearly about user input (codes like input.invalid, prompt.too_long). That helps sample-apps show inline validation instead of a global error modal.
Kira: Also important: streaming endpoints can close mid-stream with a 499 or connection reset. We should have StreamError that includes final status (if any), request_id, and a hint (e.g. 'Try resuming the stream' or 'Shorten your prompt').
Ben: Concrete metadata shape (flat keys only): status, code, retryable, retry_after, hint, request_id. Keep everything as simple strings/bools. No nested objects.
Sofia: Example pseudo mapping at transport boundary I sketched:
```
body = parse_json(resp.body or "{}")
meta = {"status": str(status), "code": body.get("code") or "", "retryable": str(status >= 500), "retry_after": resp.headers.get("Retry-After",""), "hint": "", "request_id": resp.headers.get("X-Request-Id",")"}
if status == 401:
    raise AuthError(body.get("message") or "authentication failed", meta)
elif status == 429:
    raise RateLimitError(body.get("message") or "rate limited", meta)
elif status == 400 and body.get("code",").startswith("input."):
    raise ClientInputError(body.get("message") or "invalid input", meta)
elif 400 <= status < 500:
    raise ClientError(body.get("message") or "client error", meta)
elif status >= 500:
    raise ServerError("server error", meta)
# streaming transport catches connection resets and wraps as StreamError with last known meta
```
Alex: Nice. A couple things: 1) include request_id in metadata so support can trace quickly, 2) default exception.__str__ should be friendly, include hint and not raw JSON unless RI_SDK_DEBUG=true.
Kira: UX: sample-app should render ClientInputError inline (field-level), AuthError -> show re-auth CTA, RateLimitError -> show retry countdown if retry_after present, StreamError -> recommend retry or shorter prompt. Hints must be short imperatives.
Ben: Tests: add parity suite that sends fake responses (status + headers + body) and asserts exception class, metadata keys, and that hint is present when applicable. We'll run across py/node/go.
Sofia: Telemetry: tag errors with error_class and error_code; for onboarding funnel we alert when ClientInputError or AuthError spikes. ops-bot can create a ticket automatically for unusual upticks.
ops-bot: (automated) created ticket INF-7002: "SDK: typed exceptions + client-input/stream error mapping for onboarding" assigned to Ben.
Alex: I'll take the py implementation: add exceptions module, attach flat metadata dict, parse Retry-After and X-Request-Id, and update sample-app rendering. ETA: 4d.
Kira: I'll update the onboarding docs and write a short snippet: example handling logic (switch on exception class -> show hint or inline validation).
Ben: I'll add parity tests and a CI job to run them on SDK PRs. Also will add a tiny e2e that simulates a malformed prompt to ensure the sample-app responds with inline validation.
Sofia: One more: avoid exposing internal codes to end users; show friendly user_message derived from hint instead. Keep code only in metadata for programmatic use.
Alex: Good point. Metadata.code stays machine-only. user_message/hint is what gets shown.
Kira: Great. Drop PR links here when ready and we'll canary to staging. This should cut onboarding confusion considerably.
Ben: Thanks — will update INF-7002 with PR and timeline. :thumbsup:
